info.text: The word “heavy” must be used as part of the identification in communications with or about heavy jet aircraft when providing airport advisories. PHRASEOLOGY - “United Fifty–Eight Heavy”

NOTE 1: Most airlines will use the word “heavy” following the company prefix and trip number when establishing communications or when changing frequencies. NOTE 2: When in radio-telephone communications with "Air Force One," do not add the heavy designator to the call sign. State only the call sign "Air Force One" regardless of the type of aircraft.
Preface a clearance or instruction intended for a specific aircraft with the identification of that aircraft. EXAMPLE “Piper Three Four Seven Seven Papa, Fort Worth Radio, ATC clearance, over.”

Emphasize appropriate digits, letters, or similar sounding words to aid in distinguishing between similar sounding aircraft identifications. Additionally, notify each pilot concerned when communicating with aircraft having similar sounding identifications.

Example "Advisory to Cessna One Three Two Four, transmissions to Cessna One Two Three Four also being made on this frequency." "American Five Twenty-one and American Twenty-one, transmissions being made to each of you on this frequency."
